entries.name: torch.Generator
entries.summary: Random number generator object that can be passed to randperm, DataLoader, etc., to get reproducible randomness independent of the global seed.
entries.returns: A Generator; .manual_seed(seed) returns the generator itself so calls can be chained.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.T
entries.summary: Transpose of a 2-D tensor (x.mT transposes the last two dims of any batch; x.t() is the method).
notes: On tensors with more than 2 dims, .T reverses ALL dims (deprecated) - use .mT or transpose(-2, -1).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.abs
entries.summary: Element-wise absolute value.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.any
entries.summary: True if any element is True (optionally along a dim).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.argmax
entries.summary: Index of the maximum value along a dimension. With dim=None the tensor is flattened first.

parameters.name: keepdim
parameters.description: Keep the reduced dim with size 1.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.argsort
entries.summary: Indices that would sort the tensor.
notes: Applying argsort twice gives each element's rank.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.backward
entries.summary: Computes gradients of this tensor w.r.t. graph leaves and accumulates them into their .grad.

parameters.name: gradient
parameters.description: Required if the tensor is not a scalar.

parameters.name: retain_graph
parameters.description: Keep the graph so backward can be called again.

notes: Usually called on a scalar loss.
Accumulates into .grad; it does not overwrite.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.chunk
entries.summary: Splits a tensor into a given NUMBER of chunks along a dimension (the last may be smaller).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.clone
entries.summary: Copy of the tensor that stays in the autograd graph.
entries.returns: A new Tensor with its own memory.
entries.example: best_state = {k: v.cpu().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
notes: Use detach().clone() for a graph-free copy.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.contiguous
entries.summary: Returns a tensor with standard row-major memory layout (copies only if needed).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.copy_
entries.summary: In-place copy of another tensor's values (broadcasting allowed).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.cpu
entries.summary: Moves a tensor to CPU memory.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.data_ptr
entries.summary: Address of the first element in memory - equal pointers mean shared storage (e.g. tied embeddings).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.detach
entries.summary: Returns a tensor sharing the data but cut from the autograd graph.
notes: Shares memory with the original.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.diag
entries.summary: Diagonal of a 2-D tensor (or a diagonal matrix from a 1-D tensor).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.dim
entries.summary: Number of dimensions (rank) of the tensor.
entries.example:
decay = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.dim() > 1]      # weights
no_decay = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.dim() <= 1]  # biases, norm scales
notes: dim()/ndimension() are methods; ndim is an attribute (no parentheses).
Common trick: parameters with ndim < 2 (biases, LayerNorm/RMSNorm scales) are excluded from weight decay.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.double
entries.summary: Casts to float64 (also on modules: model.double()).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.expand
entries.summary: Broadcasts size-1 dimensions to a larger size without copying (-1 keeps a dimension).
notes: Result shares memory - don't write into it in place.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.flip
entries.summary: Reverses the order of elements along the given dimensions.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.float
entries.summary: Casts to float32.
entries.returns: A float32 Tensor (self if already float32).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.int
entries.summary: Casts to int32.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.item
entries.summary: Python number from a one-element tensor.
notes: Forces a GPU sync and detaches from the graph - don't accumulate tensors in logs.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.long
entries.summary: Casts to int64.
notes: Index tensors must be int64 (or bool).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.masked_fill
entries.summary: Returns a copy where positions with mask == True are replaced by a value.
entries.returns: A new Tensor (masked_fill_ is the in-place version).
notes: Fills where the mask is True - invert with ~ if your mask marks the entries to KEEP.
-inf before softmax gives exactly zero weight.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.masked_fill_
entries.summary: In-place version of masked_fill: overwrites the tensor where mask is True and returns it.

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Broadcastable to the tensor; True = overwrite.

notes: Mutates the caller: `masked = scores.masked_fill_(...)` makes `masked` and `scores` the same tensor.
In-place ops on tensors autograd needs for backward can raise an error; prefer masked_fill.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.max
entries.summary: Maximum value; with dim returns (values, indices).
entries.returns: Tensor, or namedtuple (values, indices) when dim is given.
notes: max reduces ONE dim; use amax for several dims.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.mean
entries.summary: Mean over all elements or over the given dimensions.
notes: Empty selections give NaN.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.min
entries.summary: Minimum value; with dim returns (values, indices).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.nanmean
entries.summary: Mean that ignores NaN entries.
notes: Used to skip classes that have no pixels (their IoU is NaN).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.new_empty
entries.summary: Uninitialised tensor with the same dtype and device as this tensor.
entries.returns: A new Tensor with arbitrary contents.
notes: Contents are garbage until written.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.new_zeros
entries.summary: Zero tensor with the same dtype and device as this tensor.
notes: new_empty is the uninitialised version - only use it if every element will be overwritten.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.numel
entries.summary: Total number of elements.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.numpy
entries.summary: Returns a NumPy array sharing memory with a CPU tensor.
notes: Needs a CPU tensor without grad: detach().cpu() first.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.permute
entries.summary: Reorders all dimensions.
entries.returns: A view with permuted strides (usually non-contiguous).
notes: The result is non-contiguous: use reshape (or .contiguous().view).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.pow
entries.summary: Element-wise power (x ** p).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.repeat
entries.summary: Repeats the tensor along each dimension (copies data).
notes: expand does the same without copying (size-1 dims only).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.reshape
entries.summary: Returns a tensor with the same data and a new shape; a view if possible, otherwise a copy.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: New shape; one dimension may be -1 (inferred).

notes: Works on non-contiguous tensors (view would raise).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.round
entries.summary: Rounds to the nearest integer (or to `decimals` digits).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.shape
entries.summary: Tuple-like torch.Size with the size of every dimension (x.size() is the method form; x.size(0) / x.shape[0] gives one dimension).
notes: Unpack shapes at the top of a function and re-use the names in reshape calls.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.squeeze
entries.summary: Removes size-1 dimensions (all of them, or the given one).

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Only squeeze this dim if its size is 1.

notes: Without dim it also removes a batch axis of size 1 - prefer squeeze(-1).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.std
entries.summary: Standard deviation; unbiased (N-1) by default.

parameters.name: unbiased
parameters.description: False divides by N (population std). Newer API: correction=0.

notes: Normalisation statistics usually use the population std (unbiased=False).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.sum
entries.summary: Sum over all elements or over the given dimensions.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Dimension(s) to reduce - they disappear from the shape.

parameters.name: keepdim
parameters.description: Keep reduced dims as size 1 so the result broadcasts against the input.

entries.example: x.sum(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)  # (N, C, H, W) -> (1, C, 1, 1)
notes: The dims you pass are the ones that get collapsed.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.to
entries.summary: Converts dtype and/or moves to a device. Returns self if nothing changes.
notes: No copy is made when dtype/device already match - the result may alias the input.
Move the labels too, not just the inputs.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.tolist
entries.summary: Converts a tensor to (nested) Python lists.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.transpose
entries.summary: Swaps two dimensions.
entries.returns: A view with those dims swapped.
notes: Non-contiguous result: follow with reshape rather than view.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.type_as
entries.summary: Casts the tensor to the dtype (and device type) of `other`.
entries.example:
m = mask[..., None].type_as(x)   # bool mask -> float like x
pooled = (x * m).sum(1) / m.sum(1)
notes: Equivalent to .to(other.dtype) for dtype; use .to(other) to also copy the device.
A bool mask must be cast before it is multiplied with float activations (or use masked_fill).

entries.name: torch.Tensor.unsqueeze
entries.summary: Inserts a size-1 dimension at the given position.
notes: x[:, None] is equivalent.

entries.name: torch.Tensor.view
entries.summary: Returns a tensor with the same data and a new shape. One dimension may be -1 (inferred).
notes: Requires contiguous memory; use reshape() if unsure.

entries.name: torch.addmm
entries.summary: Fused input + mat1 @ mat2: a linear layer in one call (bias is broadcast over rows).
entries.returns: Tensor (n, p) for mat1 (n, m) and mat2 (m, p).
entries.example: logits = torch.addmm(b, images, W)   # b: (C,), images: (N, D), W: (D, C)

entries.name: torch.allclose
entries.summary: True if all elements are close within rtol/atol.

entries.name: torch.amax
entries.summary: Maximum over one or several dimensions, values only (no indices).
entries.example:
x.amax(dim=(-2, -1))  # max-pool a window
logits - logits.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # stable softmax shift
notes: Faster than max(dim) when you don't need the indices; evenly distributes gradient among ties.

entries.name: torch.arange
entries.summary: 1-D tensor of evenly spaced values in [start, end) with the given step.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: int64 if all arguments are integers, otherwise the default float dtype.

entries.returns: 1-D Tensor of length ceil((end - start) / step).
entries.example:
torch.arange(4)                        # tensor([0, 1, 2, 3])
torch.arange(0, 1, 0.25)               # tensor([0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75])
torch.arange(6, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(2, 3)
notes: Integer arguments give an int64 tensor - pass dtype=... if you need floats.
Pass device=x.device when building index tensors for GPU data.

entries.name: torch.as_tensor
entries.summary: Converts data to a tensor, avoiding a copy when dtype/device already match (shares memory with ndarray inputs).

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Optional cast (copies if it changes the dtype).

entries.returns: A Tensor, possibly sharing memory with data.
notes: Not a safe way to get an independent copy: add .clone().

entries.name: torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark
entries.summary: If True, cuDNN auto-tunes convolution algorithms (faster for fixed shapes, non-deterministic).

entries.name: torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic
entries.summary: If True, cuDNN only uses deterministic algorithms (reproducible but possibly slower).

entries.name: torch.bincount
entries.summary: Counts occurrences of each non-negative integer in a 1-D tensor.

parameters.name: minlength
parameters.description: Minimum length of the output (use K*K for a confusion matrix).

entries.example:
idx = target.reshape(-1) * K + pred.reshape(-1)
cm = torch.bincount(idx, minlength=K * K).reshape(K, K)

entries.name: torch.block_diag
entries.summary: Builds a block-diagonal matrix from the given matrices.

entries.name: torch.bmm
entries.summary: Batched matrix product of two 3-D tensors (N, a, b) x (N, b, c).

entries.name: torch.bool
entries.summary: Boolean dtype, used for masks.
notes: Invert with ~mask.

entries.name: torch.cat
entries.summary: Concatenates tensors along an EXISTING dimension.

parameters.name: tensors
parameters.description: Tensors with equal shapes except along dim.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Dimension to join, e.g. 1 for channels in NCHW.

entries.example: u = torch.cat([skip, up], dim=1)  # (N, C1+C2, H, W)
notes: torch.concat is an alias.
Order matters when later layers expect a particular channel order.

entries.name: torch.cdist
entries.summary: Pairwise distances between row sets (p-norm).
notes: Forbidden in the Project 1 exercise: implement the ||a||^2 - 2a.b + ||b||^2 expansion instead.

entries.name: torch.clamp
entries.summary: Limits values to the range [min, max].
notes: Pass at least one of min/max.

entries.name: torch.cos
entries.summary: Element-wise cosine (radians).

entries.name: torch.cuda.empty_cache
entries.summary: Releases unused cached GPU memory back to the driver.
notes: Doesn't free tensors that are still referenced.

entries.name: torch.cuda.get_device_name
entries.summary: Name of a GPU, e.g. 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti'.

entries.name: torch.cuda.is_available
entries.summary: True if a CUDA GPU can be used.

entries.name: torch.cuda.manual_seed
entries.summary: Seeds the random number generator of the current GPU only.
notes: torch.cuda.manual_seed_all seeds every GPU; torch.manual_seed already seeds CUDA lazily in recent versions.
Silently ignored if CUDA is not available.

entries.name: torch.cuda.manual_seed_all
entries.summary: Seeds the random number generators of all GPUs.

entries.name: torch.cuda.synchronize
entries.summary: Waits for all queued GPU kernels to finish - needed for accurate timings.

entries.name: torch.device
entries.summary: Describes where tensors live ('cpu', 'cuda', 'cuda:1').

entries.name: torch.einsum
entries.summary: Einstein-summation: multiply and sum tensors according to an index equation.

parameters.name: equation
parameters.description: e.g. 'nc,cokh->nokh'; indices missing from the output are summed.

entries.example: stamp = torch.einsum('nc,cokh->nokh', x[:, :, i, j], weight)
notes: Index appears on the left but not on the right -> multiply and sum over it.

entries.name: torch.enable_grad
entries.summary: Re-enables gradient tracking inside a block, even when an outer no_grad / set_grad_enabled(False) is active. Also works as a decorator.
notes: Does not override torch.inference_mode.
Typical use: a training function that may be called from inside an evaluation loop wrapped in no_grad.

entries.name: torch.equal
entries.summary: True if two tensors have the same shape and exactly equal elements.
notes: Exact comparison; use torch.allclose for floats.

entries.name: torch.exp
entries.summary: Element-wise e^x.

entries.name: torch.eye
entries.summary: 2-D identity matrix.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Rows (and columns if m is None).

entries.returns: (n, m) Tensor with ones on the diagonal.

entries.name: torch.flatten
entries.summary: Flattens dimensions start_dim..end_dim into one. Use start_dim=1 to keep the batch dimension.

entries.name: torch.float32
entries.summary: 32-bit floating point dtype (the default float dtype).
notes: torch.float is an alias.

entries.name: torch.float64
entries.summary: 64-bit floating point dtype; use it to compare an implementation against PyTorch with tight tolerances.
notes: torch.double is an alias.

entries.name: torch.floor
entries.summary: Element-wise floor.

entries.name: torch.from_numpy
entries.summary: Creates a tensor that SHARES memory with a NumPy array (no copy). dtype and shape come from the array.

parameters.name: ndarray
parameters.description: Source array (must have a supported dtype).

entries.returns: A Tensor viewing the array's buffer.
entries.example:
a = np.zeros(3)
t = torch.from_numpy(a)
t += 1
print(a)  # [1. 1. 1.]
notes: Mutating either object changes the other.
Keeps the array's dtype (float64 stays float64); chain .to(torch.float32) AND .clone() if you need an independent float32 copy.

entries.name: torch.full
entries.summary: Tensor of the given shape filled with one value.

parameters.name: fill_value
parameters.description: Value (dtype is inferred from it unless given).

entries.name: torch.full_like
entries.summary: Tensor filled with a value, with the shape/dtype/device of the input.

entries.name: torch.gather
entries.summary: Picks values along one dimension using an index tensor of the same number of dimensions; output has the shape of index.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Same number of dims as input; values index into input along dim.

entries.returns: Tensor with the shape of index.
entries.example:
log_probs = torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=1)      # (N, K)
picked = torch.gather(log_probs, 1, labels.unsqueeze(1))  # (N, 1)
notes: For dim=1: out[i][j] = input[i][index[i][j]].
Add a singleton axis to the labels (unsqueeze) so index has the same rank as input; squeeze afterwards if needed.

entries.name: torch.get_num_threads
entries.summary: Current number of CPU threads used for intra-op parallelism.

entries.name: torch.hub.load_state_dict_from_url
entries.summary: Downloads (and caches) a checkpoint file from a URL and loads it.

entries.name: torch.index_select
entries.summary: Selects entries along one dimension using a 1-D LongTensor of indices (rows of an embedding matrix, for instance).

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Indices to take; must be a tensor, not a Python list.

entries.returns: Tensor with size len(index) along dim.
entries.example: rows = emb_weight.index_select(0, torch.tensor([3, 1, 4]))   # same as emb_weight[[3, 1, 4]]
notes: Plain advanced indexing x[idx] does the same for dim 0.
Unlike gather, index is 1-D and picks whole slices.

entries.name: torch.inf
entries.summary: Positive infinity as a Python float (same as float("inf")); use -torch.inf for masked attention scores.
notes: softmax of a row that is entirely -inf gives NaN; keep at least one valid key per query.
-inf (not a large negative like -1e9 in fp16) gives exactly zero attention weight.

entries.name: torch.inference_mode
entries.summary: Like no_grad but stricter and faster: tensors created inside cannot be used in autograd later.
notes: Does not switch layers to eval mode.

entries.name: torch.int64
entries.summary: 64-bit integer dtype; required for class labels and index tensors.
notes: torch.long is an alias.

entries.name: torch.isfinite
entries.summary: Boolean mask: True where values are neither NaN nor +-inf.

entries.name: torch.isinf
entries.summary: Boolean mask: True where values are +-inf.

entries.name: torch.linspace
entries.summary: 1-D tensor of `steps` evenly spaced values from start to end, both included.

entries.name: torch.load
entries.summary: Loads an object saved with torch.save.

parameters.name: weights_only
parameters.description: Restricts unpickling to tensors and primitive containers (safer).

notes: Only load files you trust.

entries.name: torch.log
entries.summary: Element-wise natural logarithm.

entries.name: torch.logical_not
entries.summary: Element-wise logical NOT; non-bool inputs are treated as True where non-zero. Always returns a bool tensor.
entries.example:
keep = mask.logical_not()   # same as ~mask for a bool mask
scores = scores.masked_fill(keep[:, None, None, :], float('-inf'))
notes: For bool masks ~mask is equivalent; ~ on an int/float tensor is NOT logical negation (it is a bitwise op / an error).

entries.name: torch.logsumexp
entries.summary: Numerically stable log(sum(exp(x))) along a dimension (internally subtracts the max before exponentiating).

parameters.name: keepdim
parameters.description: Keep the reduced dim as size 1 so the result broadcasts back against the input.

entries.returns: Tensor with the reduced dim removed (or size 1 with keepdim=True).
entries.example:
# manual cross-entropy: log p = z - logsumexp(z)
z = logits - logits.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
log_p = z - torch.logsumexp(z, dim=1, keepdim=True)
loss = -log_p.gather(1, labels.unsqueeze(1)).mean()
notes: Use keepdim=True when you subtract the result from the original (N, C) tensor.
log_softmax(z) == z - logsumexp(z, dim=-1, keepdim=True).

entries.name: torch.manual_seed
entries.summary: Seeds the global random number generator (CPU and, on recent versions, all CUDA devices).
notes: Also seed Python's random and NumPy if you use them; GPU kernels can still be non-deterministic.

entries.name: torch.matmul
entries.summary: Matrix product with broadcasting: 1-D dot, 2-D matmul, or batched matmul over leading dimensions. The @ operator calls it.
entries.example: out = w_row @ cols  # (C_out, K) @ (N, K, L) -> (N, C_out, L)
notes: The last two dims are the matrix dims; earlier dims are batch dims and broadcast.
torch.mm is strictly 2-D; torch.bmm is strictly 3-D.

entries.name: torch.median
entries.summary: Median of all values; for an even count, the LOWER of the two middle values.

entries.name: torch.meshgrid
entries.summary: Coordinate grids from 1-D tensors. Use indexing='ij' for matrix (row, column) ordering.
notes: Always pass indexing explicitly.

entries.name: torch.mm
entries.summary: Matrix product of two 2-D tensors (no broadcasting).

entries.name: torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss
entries.summary: Module form of binary_cross_entropy_with_logits: sigmoid + BCE on raw logits with 0/1 float targets (numerically stable).

parameters.name: pos_weight
parameters.description: Weight on the positive class, useful for imbalanced data.

notes: Do not put a sigmoid in the model and then use this loss (sigmoid would be applied twice).
Targets must be float and the same shape as the logits.

entries.name: torch.nn.BatchNorm2d
entries.summary: Normalises each channel over the batch and spatial dims, then applies a learnable scale (weight) and shift (bias).
notes: Train mode uses batch statistics and updates running averages; eval mode uses the running averages.
Convolutions before a BatchNorm don't need a bias.

entries.name: torch.nn.Conv2d
entries.summary: 2-D convolution (cross-correlation) over (N, C_in, H, W) inputs.
entries.signature: torch.nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=1, padding=0, dilation=1, groups=1, bias=True)

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: Learn a bias (redundant right before BatchNorm).

entries.returns: Tensor (N, C_out, H_out, W_out) with H_out = floor((H + 2p - d(k-1) - 1) / s) + 1.
notes: kernel 3 + padding 1 + stride 1 keeps H and W.
Weight shape: (out_channels, in_channels, kH, kW).

entries.name: torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d
entries.summary: Transposed convolution - learnable upsampling. Each input pixel scatters a scaled copy of the filter into the output.
entries.signature: torch.nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=1, padding=0, output_padding=0, bias=True)
entries.example: up = nn.ConvTranspose2d(64, 32, kernel_size=2, stride=2)  # doubles H and W
notes: Weight shape is (in_channels, out_channels, kH, kW) - the reverse of Conv2d.

entries.name: torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss
entries.summary: Softmax + negative log-likelihood in one. Takes raw logits and integer class indices.
entries.example:
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
loss = criterion(logits, labels)  # logits (N, C), labels (N,) int64
notes: Do NOT apply softmax before this loss.

entries.name: torch.nn.Dropout
entries.summary: Randomly zeroes elements with probability p during training (and rescales the rest); identity in eval mode.
notes: Disabled by model.eval().

entries.name: torch.nn.Embedding
entries.summary: Lookup table mapping integer ids to learnable vectors.
entries.returns: (*, embedding_dim) Tensor for an int64 input of shape (*).

entries.name: torch.nn.Flatten
entries.summary: Flattens all dims from start_dim (default 1, keeping the batch dim) to end_dim into one; the layer form of x.flatten(1).
entries.returns: (N, C*H*W) for an (N, C, H, W) input.
notes: No parameters. The in_features of the next Linear must equal C*H*W.
Unlike torch.flatten, the default start_dim is 1, not 0.

entries.name: torch.nn.GELU
entries.summary: Gaussian Error Linear Unit activation: x * Phi(x), a smooth ReLU.

entries.name: torch.nn.Identity
entries.summary: Layer that returns its input unchanged - a placeholder for optional layers.
entries.example: self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(c) if use_bn else nn.Identity()

entries.name: torch.nn.LayerNorm
entries.summary: Normalises over the last dimension(s) of each sample, then applies learnable scale and shift.

parameters.name: normalized_shape
parameters.description: Size of the trailing dimension(s) to normalise.

notes: Independent of batch size, unlike BatchNorm.

entries.name: torch.nn.Linear
entries.summary: Fully connected layer: y = x @ W.T + b. Applied to the last dimension of the input.

parameters.name: in_features
parameters.description: Size of each input sample (last dim).

notes: Input must be (*, in_features); flatten images first.
layer.weight has shape (out_features, in_features).

entries.name: torch.nn.MSELoss
entries.summary: Mean squared error between prediction and target. Call as criterion(pred, target).
notes: pred and target should have the same shape, otherwise broadcasting may silently give a wrong loss.

entries.name: torch.nn.MaxPool2d
entries.summary: Takes the max over sliding windows of each channel independently. No learnable parameters; channels are unchanged.
entries.returns: (N, C, floor((H + 2p - k) / s) + 1, floor((W + 2p - k) / s) + 1).
entries.example: pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2)   # (N, C, H, W) -> (N, C, H//2, W//2) for even H, W
notes: The floor means odd sizes drop the last row/column (e.g. 5 -> 2 with k=2).
0 parameters.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module
entries.summary: Base class of all networks and layers. Attributes that are modules/Parameters/buffers are registered automatically.
notes: Call super().__init__() first.
Call model(x), not model.forward(x), so hooks run.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.eval
entries.summary: Puts the module and its children in evaluation mode (dropout off, batch-norm uses running statistics). Equivalent to train(False).
notes: Call model.train() to go back to training mode.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.load_state_dict
entries.summary: Copies parameters and buffers from a state dict into the module.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.modules
entries.summary: Iterator over the module itself and all submodules, recursively.
entries.example:
for m in model.modules():
    if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d): ...

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.named_parameters
entries.summary: Like parameters() but yields (name, parameter) pairs, e.g. 'layer1.0.conv1.weight'.
notes: Useful to give pretrained/encoder parameters a different learning rate.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.parameters
entries.summary: Iterator over all learnable parameters (recursively).
entries.example:
optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
n = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.register_buffer
entries.summary: Registers a tensor that moves with the module (.to / .cuda) but is not a parameter.

parameters.name: persistent
parameters.description: False keeps it out of state_dict.

notes: Use for fixed tables, running statistics, masks.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.register_forward_hook
entries.summary: Registers a function called after forward with (module, input, output).
entries.example:
h = layer.register_forward_hook(lambda m, i, o: print(o.shape))
model(x)
h.remove()

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.state_dict
entries.summary: Ordered dict of all parameters and persistent buffers.
entries.example: best_state = {k: v.cpu().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
notes: Values alias the live parameters: clone (or deepcopy) to keep a snapshot.

entries.name: torch.nn.Module.train
entries.summary: Sets training mode (dropout active, batch norm uses batch statistics).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: False is the same as eval().

notes: Call it again after evaluating - eval() persists.

entries.name: torch.nn.ModuleList
entries.summary: List of modules that are properly registered (parameters tracked, saved, moved to device). It has no forward.
notes: A plain Python list hides its modules from PyTorch.

entries.name: torch.nn.MultiheadAttention
entries.summary: Multi-head attention layer (projects Q, K, V, attends, projects the output).

parameters.name: batch_first
parameters.description: Use (N, P, D) instead of (P, N, D).

parameters.name: key_padding_mask
parameters.description: forward argument (N, P): True marks keys to IGNORE - the opposite of a 'real token' mask.

entries.example:
mha = nn.MultiheadAttention(16, 4, batch_first=True)
out, w = mha(x, x, x, key_padding_mask=~mask, average_attn_weights=False)
notes: Packed projection weights are in.in_proj_weight / in_proj_bias; output projection is out_proj.

entries.name: torch.nn.NLLLoss
entries.summary: Negative log-likelihood loss: expects LOG-probabilities (e.g. from log_softmax) and class indices.
notes: CrossEntropyLoss = log_softmax + NLLLoss.

entries.name: torch.nn.Parameter
entries.summary: Tensor wrapper that marks data as a learnable parameter of a Module.
notes: A plain tensor attribute is not trained, not moved by .to(), and not saved.

entries.name: torch.nn.PixelShuffle
entries.summary: Rearranges (N, C*r^2, H, W) into (N, C, H*r, W*r) - sub-pixel upsampling.

entries.name: torch.nn.ReLU
entries.summary: Rectified linear unit module: max(0, x). Has no parameters, so it adds nothing to a parameter count and does not change the shape.
notes: Parameter-free layers (ReLU, MaxPool2d, Flatten, Dropout) contribute 0 to the count.

entries.name: torch.nn.Sequential
entries.summary: Container that applies modules one after another.
notes: Unpack a Python list with nn.Sequential(*layers).

entries.name: torch.nn.TransformerEncoderLayer
entries.summary: One transformer encoder block: self-attention + feed-forward, each with residual and LayerNorm (post-norm by default, pre-norm with norm_first=True).
entries.signature: torch.nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model, nhead, dim_feedforward=2048, dropout=0.1, activation='relu', batch_first=False, norm_first=False)
entries.example: layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(16, 1, dim_feedforward=64, dropout=0.0, activation='gelu', batch_first=True, norm_first=True)

entries.name: torch.nn.Upsample
entries.summary: Resizes by a scale factor or to a size with a chosen interpolation mode.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d
entries.summary: Average pooling to a fixed output size regardless of the input size.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy
entries.summary: Binary cross-entropy on PROBABILITIES in [0, 1] (after a sigmoid). Less stable than the with_logits version.
notes: Passing raw logits raises an error or gives wrong values; passing sigmoid(logits) to the with_logits variant is the opposite bug.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits
entries.summary: Sigmoid + binary cross-entropy from raw logits and 0/1 float targets (stable).

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Same shape as input, float in [0, 1].

notes: Don't pass sigmoid(logits).

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.conv2d
entries.summary: Functional 2-D convolution (cross-correlation) with explicit weight tensor.
entries.signature: torch.nn.functional.conv2d(input, weight, bias=None, stride=1, padding=0, dilation=1, groups=1)
notes: No filter flipping: it is a correlation.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.conv_transpose2d
entries.summary: Functional transposed convolution.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy
entries.summary: Softmax + negative log-likelihood from RAW logits and integer class targets; also works per pixel for (N, C, H, W) logits and (N, H, W) targets.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Raw scores (N, C) or (N, C, d1, ...).

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Per-class weights; the 'mean' reduction divides by the sum of used weights.

notes: Never apply softmax first.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.gelu
entries.summary: GELU activation x * Phi(x).

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.interpolate
entries.summary: Resizes a batch of images (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, ...).
entries.signature: torch.nn.functional.interpolate(input, size=None, scale_factor=None, mode='nearest', align_corners=None, antialias=False)

parameters.name: align_corners
parameters.description: False aligns pixel centres, True aligns corner pixels.

notes: Use mode='nearest' (or 'nearest-exact') for label masks so classes aren't blended.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.log_softmax
entries.summary: log(softmax(x)) computed in a numerically stable way.
notes: Better than log(softmax(x)), which underflows for confident predictions.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.max_pool2d
entries.summary: 2-D max pooling.
entries.example: F.max_pool2d(x, kernel_size=2, stride=2)  # halves H and W

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.one_hot
entries.summary: One-hot encodes an int64 tensor by appending a class dimension.
entries.example: Y = F.one_hot(target, K).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).to(P.dtype)  # (N, H, W) -> (N, K, H, W)
notes: The class axis is LAST; permute it to dim 1 for NCHW, and cast to float.

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.pixel_shuffle
entries.summary: Functional PixelShuffle: (*, C*r^2, H, W) -> (*, C, H*r, W*r).

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.relu
entries.summary: Rectified linear unit: max(0, x).

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.silu
entries.summary: SiLU / swish activation: x * sigmoid(x).

entries.name: torch.nn.functional.softmax
entries.summary: Softmax over a dimension.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Dimension that sums to 1 (always pass it).

entries.example: P = F.softmax(logits, dim=1)  # class axis of (N, K, H, W)

entries.name: torch.nn.init.kaiming_normal_
entries.summary: He initialisation: normal with variance 2/fan, suited to ReLU networks.

entries.name: torch.nn.init.normal_
entries.summary: Fills a tensor with N(mean, std^2) values in place.

entries.name: torch.nn.init.ones_
entries.summary: Fills a tensor with 1 in place.

entries.name: torch.nn.init.xavier_normal_
entries.summary: Glorot initialisation with a normal distribution.

entries.name: torch.nn.init.xavier_uniform_
entries.summary: Glorot initialisation: uniform with variance 2 / (fan_in + fan_out).

entries.name: torch.nn.init.zeros_
entries.summary: Fills a tensor with 0 in place.

entries.name: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_
entries.summary: Rescales gradients in place so their global L2 norm is at most max_norm; returns the norm measured BEFORE clipping.
notes: Call after backward() and before step().

entries.name: torch.no_grad
entries.summary: Disables gradient tracking inside the block. Saves memory and time during inference.
notes: Does NOT change layer behaviour (dropout, batch-norm); use model.eval() for that.

entries.name: torch.ones
entries.summary: Tensor filled with 1. Default dtype is float32 unless dtype is given.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Shape, as separate ints or one tuple.

notes: Create on the right device: dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device (or use x.new_zeros).

entries.name: torch.ones_like
entries.summary: Tensor of ones with the same shape, dtype and device as the input (dtype can be overridden).

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Override, e.g. torch.bool for an all-True mask.

entries.name: torch.optim.Adam
entries.summary: Adam optimiser: per-parameter adaptive step sizes from running estimates of the gradient's first and second moments. weight_decay is classic L2.

entries.name: torch.optim.AdamW
entries.summary: Adam with DECOUPLED weight decay (applied directly to the weights, not through the gradient).

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Parameters or groups such as [{'params': decay, 'weight_decay': 0.01}, {'params': other, 'weight_decay': 0.0}].

notes: Normally exclude biases and norm parameters from weight decay.

entries.name: torch.optim.Optimizer.step
entries.summary: Performs one parameter update using the gradients currently stored in .grad.
notes: Call after loss.backward().

entries.name: torch.optim.Optimizer.zero_grad
entries.summary: Resets the gradients of all tensors the optimizer manages.

parameters.name: set_to_none
parameters.description: Set .grad to None instead of filling with zeros (faster, less memory).

notes: Gradients ACCUMULATE across backward() calls; call this once per step, before backward().

entries.name: torch.optim.SGD
entries.signature: torch.optim.SGD(params, lr=0.001, momentum=0, dampening=0, weight_decay=0, nesterov=False)
entries.summary: Stochastic gradient descent optimizer, optionally with momentum.

entries.name: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR
entries.summary: Anneals the learning rate from its initial value to eta_min along half a cosine over T_max steps.

parameters.name: T_max
parameters.description: Number of scheduler steps for the half-cosine, e.g. the number of epochs.

notes: Call scheduler.step() once per period (epoch here), AFTER optimizer.step().

entries.name: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler.get_last_lr
entries.summary: List with the most recently computed learning rate of each parameter group.
notes: Read it BEFORE scheduler.step() to log the LR actually used in this epoch.

entries.name: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler.step
entries.summary: Advances the schedule by one step and updates the optimiser's learning rates.
notes: Per epoch or per batch depending on how the schedule was defined.

entries.name: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR
entries.summary: Sets lr = base_lr * lr_lambda(step), for fully custom schedules such as warm-up + cosine.

parameters.name: lr_lambda
parameters.description: Function of the step index returning a multiplier.

entries.example: sched = LambdaLR(opt, lambda s: min(1.0, (s + 1) / warmup))

entries.name: torch.outer
entries.summary: Outer product of two 1-D tensors: out[i, j] = a[i] * b[j].
notes: Alias: torch.ger.

entries.name: torch.rand
entries.summary: Tensor with values drawn uniformly from [0, 1).

entries.name: torch.randint
entries.summary: Integer tensor with values drawn uniformly from [low, high).

entries.name: torch.randn
entries.summary: Tensor with values drawn from the standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
notes: Seed with torch.manual_seed for reproducibility.

entries.name: torch.randn_like
entries.summary: Standard-normal tensor with the shape/dtype/device of the input.

entries.name: torch.randperm
entries.summary: Random permutation of the integers 0 .. n-1.

parameters.name: generator
parameters.description: Seeded generator for a reproducible shuffle.

entries.example:
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)
perm = torch.randperm(5000, generator=g)
train_idx, val_idx = perm[:4500].tolist(), perm[4500:].tolist()
notes: Indices only: slice it to split a dataset without reordering the data.

entries.name: torch.reciprocal
entries.summary: Element-wise 1 / x.
notes: torch.rsqrt(v) is the fused equivalent of reciprocal(sqrt(v)).

entries.name: torch.rsqrt
entries.summary: Element-wise 1/sqrt(x).

entries.name: torch.save
entries.summary: Serialises an object (state_dict, checkpoint dict, tensors) to disk.
notes: Save model.state_dict() rather than the whole module.

entries.name: torch.set_grad_enabled
entries.summary: Turns gradient tracking on or off from a boolean; usable as a context manager or as a global switch.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: True = track gradients, False = do not.

notes: One function for a shared train/eval code path; set_grad_enabled(False) is equivalent to no_grad.

entries.name: torch.set_num_threads
entries.summary: Sets the number of CPU threads used for intra-op parallelism.

entries.name: torch.sigmoid
entries.summary: Logistic function 1 / (1 + e^-x), mapping logits to probabilities in (0, 1).
notes: Do NOT apply it before binary_cross_entropy_with_logits (that loss applies it internally).

entries.name: torch.sin
entries.summary: Element-wise sine (radians).

entries.name: torch.softmax
entries.summary: Softmax over a dimension: exp(x_i) / sum_j exp(x_j).
notes: Don't apply before CrossEntropyLoss / F.cross_entropy - they expect raw logits.

entries.name: torch.split
entries.summary: Splits a tensor into chunks of a given SIZE (or list of sizes) along a dimension.

parameters.name: split_size_or_sections
parameters.description: Size of each chunk, or explicit sizes.

entries.example: q, k, v = qkv.split(D, dim=-1)  # three (N, P, D) pieces from (N, P, 3D)
notes: split takes the chunk SIZE, chunk takes the NUMBER of chunks.

entries.name: torch.sqrt
entries.summary: Element-wise square root.

entries.name: torch.square
entries.summary: Element-wise x**2.

entries.name: torch.stack
entries.summary: Joins tensors along a NEW dimension (all inputs must have identical shapes).
entries.returns: A new Tensor with one more dimension.

entries.name: torch.tensor
entries.summary: Builds a new tensor by COPYING data (list, scalar, NumPy array, ...). The dtype is inferred unless given.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: Force a dtype, e.g. torch.float32. Default: inferred (Python floats -> float32, ints -> int64).

entries.returns: A new Tensor that does not share memory with data.
entries.example:
a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
t = torch.tensor(a, dtype=torch.float32)
a[0] = 99
print(t)  # tensor([1., 2., 3.]) - unaffected
notes: Always copies; use torch.from_numpy / torch.as_tensor if you want to share memory.
torch.tensor(some_tensor) warns - use some_tensor.detach().clone() instead.

entries.name: torch.tensordot
entries.summary: Contracts the given dimensions of two tensors.

entries.name: torch.testing.assert_close
entries.summary: Raises with a detailed message unless two tensors match in shape, dtype, device and values (within tolerance).

entries.name: torch.topk
entries.summary: The k largest entries along a dimension, sorted from largest to smallest.

entries.name: torch.uint8
entries.summary: Unsigned 8-bit integer dtype (raw image bytes).
notes: Integer division/overflow traps: convert to float before scaling to [0, 1].

entries.name: torch.utils.data.DataLoader
entries.summary: Iterates a dataset in (optionally shuffled) mini-batches, optionally with worker processes.
entries.signature: torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=1, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, collate_fn=None, pin_memory=False, generator=None)

parameters.name: shuffle
parameters.description: True for training, False for validation/test.

parameters.name: collate_fn
parameters.description: Builds a batch from a list of samples, e.g. to pad sequences.

entries.example: loader = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=128, shuffle=True, num_workers=2, pin_memory=torch.cuda.is_available())
notes: The last batch can be smaller - weight metrics by the actual batch size.

entries.name: torch.utils.data.Dataset
entries.summary: Abstract map-style dataset: implement __len__ and __getitem__.

entries.name: torch.utils.data.Subset
entries.summary: View of a dataset restricted to the given indices.
notes: Build two base datasets with different transforms (train/eval) and wrap each in a Subset with disjoint indices.

entries.name: torch.vstack
entries.summary: Concatenates along dim 0 after promoting 1-D tensors to rows (like torch.cat(dim=0) but 1-D inputs become (1, n)).
notes: torch.cat is the more explicit choice when every input already has a leading dim.

entries.name: torch.where
entries.summary: Element-wise choice: takes values from x where condition is True and from y elsewhere.
notes: Selects instead of multiplying, so NaN/inf in discarded entries cannot leak (NaN * 0 is NaN).

entries.name: torch.zeros
entries.summary: Tensor filled with 0. Default dtype is float32 unless dtype is given.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Shape, as separate ints or one tuple.

notes: Create on the right device: dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device (or use x.new_zeros).

entries.name: torch.zeros_like
entries.summary: Zero tensor with the same shape, dtype and device as the input.

entries.name: torchvision.datasets.OxfordIIITPet
entries.summary: Oxford-IIIT Pet dataset (37 breeds) with optional segmentation trimaps.

entries.name: torchvision.datasets.STL10
entries.summary: STL-10 dataset of 96x96 colour images in 10 classes (5,000 labelled train, 8,000 test).

entries.name: torchvision.models.ResNet18_Weights
entries.summary: Enum of available pretrained weights for resnet18; IMAGENET1K_V1 is the classic ImageNet checkpoint.

entries.name: torchvision.models.resnet18
entries.summary: ResNet-18 architecture, optionally with pretrained ImageNet weights.

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: e.g. ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1; None gives random init.

entries.returns: A torch.nn.Module with conv1, bn1, relu, maxpool, layer1-4, avgpool, fc.
entries.example:
backbone = torchvision.models.resnet18(weights=None)
stem = nn.Sequential(backbone.conv1, backbone.bn1, backbone.relu)
notes: The stages' strides: stem /2, pool /4, layer2 /8, layer3 /16, layer4 /32.

entries.name: torchvision.transforms.Compose
entries.summary: Chains transforms in the order given.
entries.example: T.Compose([T.RandomCrop(96, padding=4), T.RandomHorizontalFlip(), T.ToTensor(), T.Normalize(mean, std)])
notes: Order matters: PIL-only transforms before ToTensor, Normalize after it.

entries.name: torchvision.transforms.Normalize
entries.summary: Per-channel standardisation of a TENSOR image: (x - mean) / std.
notes: Must come after ToTensor; to visualise, invert with x * std + mean.

entries.name: torchvision.transforms.RandomCrop
entries.summary: Crops a random window; with padding it first pads the image (padding_mode='reflect' mirrors the border).
notes: Training-time augmentation only.

entries.name: torchvision.transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip
entries.summary: Flips the image left-right with probability p.
notes: Training-time augmentation only.

entries.name: torchvision.transforms.ToTensor
entries.summary: Converts a PIL image / HWC uint8 array into a CHW float32 tensor scaled to [0, 1].

entries.name: torchvision.utils.make_grid
entries.summary: Tiles a batch of images (N, C, H, W) into one image grid.
notes: Un-normalise (x*std + mean) before showing normalised images.
